title: Data Access and Management
topicSummary: SQL, APIs, web scraping, data cleaning, cloud storage.

content.text: After learning what data is (Week 2), this module focuses on how to access, retrieve, process, and store urban data efficiently.
Core Pipeline: Data Sources → Access (SQL/APIs/Scraping) → Cleaning → Storage (Cloud)
Definition: SQL is used to query and manipulate data stored in relational databases.

content.code:
-- Example Query
SELECT location, AVG(speed)
FROM traffic_data
WHERE time = '08:00'
GROUP BY location;

content.text: 👉 This calculates average speed per location at a specific time.

📖 Reading Note: A practical SQL example for urban analysis — HMDA (Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority) stores all building permit approvals in a PostgreSQL database. A city planner can run: SELECT zone, COUNT(*) FROM permits WHERE status='approved' AND year=2023 GROUP BY zone ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC; — to instantly see which zones had maximum construction approvals in 2023, informing decisions about infrastructure upgrades needed in those areas. SQL is the direct language of urban data governance.
Definition: APIs allow systems to communicate and exchange data programmatically.
👉 Instead of manually downloading data, you request it via API.

📖 Reading Note: The Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) is a free, open weather data API that returns historical and forecast weather for any city. URL format: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=12.97&longitude=77.59&hourly=temperature_2m — this returns hourly temperature data for Bengaluru. Urban researchers use this exact API to study the correlation between temperature spikes and water consumption peaks in distribution networks. No signup or API key needed — great for learning.
Definition: Web scraping is the process of extracting data from websites automatically.

items: Data is publicly displayed on websites

content.code:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import requests
html = requests.get("https://example.com").text
soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
data = soup.find_all("table")

content.text: 📖 Reading Note: A real urban research application of web scraping: Researchers at IIT Bombay scraped property listing prices from 99acres.com for Mumbai neighborhoods every week for 2 years. By analyzing price trends alongside scraped metro station announcements and scraped construction zone notices, they built a land-value prediction model with 82% accuracy — without any official government data. Always check a site's robots.txt (e.g., https://99acres.com/robots.txt) before scraping to verify what's permitted.

content.text: 📖 Reading Note: In practice, data scientists spend ~60-80% of project time on data cleaning. A well-known urban data cleaning challenge: Bengaluru BMTC GPS data frequently has coordinates of (0.0, 0.0) — which is the middle of the Atlantic Ocean — due to GPS signal dropout. A proper cleaning step removes these 'null island' readings. Another common issue: sensor timestamps use different formats ('28-Apr-2024' vs '2024/04/28') depending on the device vendor — standardization to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) is best practice.
Definition: Cloud storage allows data to be stored and accessed over the internet.
Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud.

📖 Reading Note: India's NITI Aayog runs Smart Cities Mission Command Centres on AWS (Amazon Web Services). Key advantage: during the COVID pandemic, cities saw 10x traffic on their health portals overnight. Because data was on cloud, they just scaled up server resources with a few clicks (elastic scaling) — something impossible with physical servers. AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service) is commonly used for archiving raw CCTV footage and satellite imagery — both unstructured data types that don't fit in traditional databases.
Traffic Monitoring System: Sensors collect vehicle data → API streams data to server → SQL queries analyze congestion → Data cleaned for accuracy → Stored in cloud for scalability.
How Week 3 Concepts Connect Across the Course:

rows: SQL cannot exist without understanding tables and keys from Week 2 — they are inseparably linked
PostGIS uses advanced SQL spatial functions (ST_Distance, ST_Buffer) — Week 3's SQL foundations enable Week 12's geospatial queries
Data fetched from APIs (as JSON) is loaded into Pandas DataFrames for analysis — Week 3 gets the data, Week 5 analyzes it
Web scraping uses Python's requests + BeautifulSoup libraries — Week 4's Python programming skills are prerequisites for scraping
Every ML model in Weeks 6–9 requires clean data as input — poor cleaning leads to garbage-in, garbage-out models. Data cleaning is the most impactful pre-ML step
IoT devices (Week 10) stream data to the same cloud platforms introduced in Week 3 — AWS/Azure/Google Cloud bridge both topics

content.text: 🔗 Big Picture: Week 3 is the practical 'data plumbing' of the course. Without being able to access and clean data, no analysis tool (Pandas, ML, IoT dashboards) can work. Every single week from 5 to 12 relies on data that first flows through the pipeline established in Week 3.
